sources.text: For 25 years, XBOX has remained focused on building games players love, and our anniversary year has been a particularly strong example. From Gears of War: E-Day , Forza Horizon 6 , and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , to hugely anticipated games like Fable , players have more great games to play on XBOX than ever. Today, The Game Awards has announced this year’s list of nominees and titles across XBOX’s creative teams have earned eight nominations across multiple categories. Outside of gaming, Prime Video’s ‘Fallout’ has been nominated for Best Adaptation. Thank you to all of the teams that brought these great games to players. Voting is now open on The Game Awards’ official site – tune into The Game Awards on December 10 to see if your favorite games from 2026 take home an award. Our publishing partners also received nominations across a range of categories, with many games available to play today with Game Pass. 007 First Light and CONTROL Resonant are both nominated for Game of the Year and playable across devices with XBOX Play Anywhere. Game Pass subscribers can play nominees like Gears of War: E-Day , Forza Horizon 6 , No Man’s Sky , and more. See below for the full list of nominees playable on XBOX, including Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , and remember you can vote for your favorites right now over at TheGameAwards.com . Congratulations to this year’s incredible nominees!

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Review
sources.text: During my first dozen-or-so hours with Grand Theft Auto 6, I fixed my leaky roof, collected some rum from a shady liquor store, played way too many games of pool, read a book about World War 2 soldiers with a penchant for teabagging, and caught a lot of fish. On the more ridiculous end of the spectrum, I also temporarily… borrowed a luxury yacht called Party on the Poop Deck before running it aground and drinking its owner’s beer, slapped the crap out of a bloke who cursed at me, found a finger in my horniest neighbour’s plumbing, threatened an alligator wearing a hat, and got mugged by a drunk sea captain with a harpoon gun – before stealing his weapon while he peed in a garden. Over 100 hours later, I’ve now completely lost track of all the things I’ve seen and done within GTA 6’s astounding open world – and I see no real limit to the amount of time I could spend here, endlessly exploring and interacting with Vice City and the massive area surrounding it. While the well-paced story effectively nudged me around the map, there are still vast sections of it that I’m yet to even visit – despite hitting the credits after almost 120 hours of hijinks. Frankly, I’ve never played anything that’s hit quite like GTA 6 – and right now I have zero plans to stop playing it. Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are an interesting pair of playable characters, and unlike any leads that have come before them in the series. Their motivations and goals are very different from the main characters of previous GTA games, and their priority is really about escape rather than revenge or empire building. They’re not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time, but the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make the couple easy to root for throughout their story – which unfolds like four or five seasons of a prestige TV show. My Jason and Lucia maintained a professional criminal rating throughout thanks to my style of play, where I opt for clean escapes, stealth, and non-lethal takedowns against general law enforcement if feasible, disabling vehicles by popping tyres rather than pummelling the windscreens with gunfire, and leaving civilians unharmed as often as possible. By the end of the story, I had actually only killed 11 civilians, all of which would’ve been unfortunate accidents. Jason, a capable yet calm and softly spoken army veteran, is a natural fit for GTA. He remains mostly a mystery throughout, but his quiet cowboy demeanour doesn’t stray too far from Red Dead Redemption 2’s Arthur Morgan, and I like that. Lucia, who’s headstrong but not abrasive and confident but not cocky, gets to showcase a wider range of emotions. She’s easily the most likeable and multifaceted woman in the history of the series, and it’s abundantly clear that GTA’s writing has grown up dramatically in the last 13 years – and that RDR2 has had nothing but positive effects on its sister series. We play mostly as Jason for the opening phase of Chapter 1, but it’s a smart way of easing us into the many systems we need to come to grips with (there’s a full help menu to explain any controls or actions you might forget). In the time it takes to start and finish many typical shooters and action games, I’d lived several days of a second life as Jason, who spends a good deal of his time on the wrong side of the law couriering drug shipments up and down the Leonida Keys but otherwise keeps a low profile in the relatively quiet tourist town he calls home. There’d been strife and there’d been shootouts, sure, but the main thread of the story had barely begun: Lucia was yet to re-enter the picture, I’d not even visited Vice City itself at all, and I was entirely content to while away hours messing around with GTA 6’s many, many distractions. It’s ironic, perhaps, that some of its greatest distractions are actually games themselves – Jason has a PlayStation-style console in his home featuring three playable games, and his local bar has a darkly humorous riff on classic Buck Hunter cabinets I kept getting sucked into. Straight away, it’s evident this is not a world of painted-on backdrops and empty props. This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I’ve ever played, and it’s one you can interact with at a level never seen before in the series. Yes, it was a long wait, but believe me when I say Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out (which, handily enough, is also something you can do yourself in GTA 6 if you find yourself beached). I’ll readily admit I’m an easy mark for a game like this. I love action movies, car chases, and dad rock, and GTA 6 holds precisely the same things near and dear. I won’t list the long catalogue of movie references I’ve spotted since it’s way more satisfying to recognise them yourself. I also won’t spoil any of the specific needle drops Rockstar finds itself indulging in more than ever – one of which has become one of my favourite moments in the entire series. It does take over the dial a bit more than usual for key moments, but it’s always to great effect, and it certainly hasn’t come at the cost of any reduced focus on radio stations. The mammoth tracklist otherwise includes the return of classic stations V-Rock, Emotion, and Vice City FM, all of which are absolutely overflowing with solid gold (as is new metal station The Chamber). Just those four stations alone – which account for the lion’s share of my listening – feature nearly 200 songs between them. In a considerable blow for any company trying to sell me a next-generation console in the near future, GTA 6 also looks even better than it sounds. Allow me to freely concede I’ve never been fussy about frame rates, so long as they don’t constantly fluctuate. sources.text: Critics praise the "richly drawn and compelling romance" of Jason and Lucia in GTA 6, delivering a record Metacritic score After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has been met with universal acclaim. Despite a lead-up marred by delays and leaks the hype has only grown, with over 17 million pre-orders generating more than $1.6 billion in revenue, according to recent data . Critics have spent weeks exploring Rockstar's Leonida, featuring the Bonnie-and-Clyde-inspired duo Jason and Lucia, leading to a Metacritic score of 99 . Backed by over 100 reviews, the title is currently listed as the platform's best game of all time , above the original N64 release of The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time. In the words of The Guardian 's Keza MacDonald: "Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have seen yet." "Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief, so vast that it feels overwhelming [...] and contains so many potential experiences that it's hard to know where to start." IGN 's Luke Reilly emphasised that the wait for GTA 6 was reflected in the detail Rockstar has poured into its world. "This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I've ever played, and it's one you can interact with at a level never seen before in the series," he said. "Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out.” The game's level of detail raised concerns about performance, particularly its 30fps cap on all consoles , including the PlayStation 5 Pro. However, Reilly found that this limitation did not diminish the experience. "What matters to me is that it looks absolutely incredible and runs smoothly and reliably on a standard PS5. I find all the brilliant visual flourishes far more important, from the concentric rings of ripples on water due to helicopter rotor downwash, to the almost imperceptible line of sweat that appears on Lucia's forehead after a brisk jog, or the buckling of the fabric on a shirt as torsos twist, to the temporary dents on a punching bag as you strike it." "If a sufficiently stable and properly paced 30fps is the route to GTA 6 looking and functioning the way it does, bug-free, then I have no complaints." GTA 6's immersion extends to daily routines that improve stats like health and stamina, or managing car fuel levels. As Game Informer 's Matt Miller observed, these activities "add pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward." These everyday moments are initially character-specific, as The New York Times' Yussef Cole noted. "Jason can opt to fix up his run-down bachelor pad in preparation for Lucia's imminent release. There are numerous tasks around the house, like putting up drywall, painting and fixing the roof, that take up the player's time and the character's in-game resources, but they aim toward a productive and satisfying goal: a better relationship." That's not to say GTA 6 isn't like past games, where violence is encouraged and chaos is one petty crime away. Miller emphasised that these moments do not detract from the "meticulously choreographed" set pieces, which "run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect." Critics agreed that GTA 6 offers unexpected emotional depth, thanks to nuance in both the representation of the lead characters and the player's ability to control them. IGN's Reilly described Jason and Lucia as "unlike any leads that have come before them in the series," whose priorities are each other and escaping the criminal life they find themselves increasingly entrenched in. "They're not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time, but the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make the couple easy to root for throughout their story,"he wrote. The New York Times' Cole agreed, adding that the emphasis on the duo's relationship "reflects a maturation of a series that has generally only told stories about men solipsistically chasing after their own success." He continued: "Choosing romance is the easy part, thanks to the chemistry and human characterisation of the two leads. Lucia and Jason's relationship builds on itself and becomes a constant, supportive presence. It gets reflected in the story missions too, as your characters make scripted choices that reflect how you behaved toward each other in the idle moments in between." Game Informer's Miller described Jason and Lucia's relationship as "elevating the game to new heights, lending this instalment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries." "This is, without a doubt, video gaming's most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you're left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts." The Guardian's MacDonald "found it impossible not to care" for the couple over time. "They are our avatars in GTA 6's world, but they are not blank stand-ins for the player: you decide their actions but not their personalities. They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim [...] When the story gave me opportunities to decide what would happen next, what came to mind for me was what they would do, not what I would do." sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker pleads guilty to all charges
sources.text: Arion Kurtaj released dozens of GTA 6 videos to the public more than a year before the game was formally revealed. The BBC reports that Arion Kurtaj, who hacked Rockstar and dumped a massive trove of content from Grand Theft Auto 6 more than a year before it was formally revealed, has pleaded guilty to that and other hacks carried out while he was a member of the Lapsus$ hacking group. Kurtaj's hack of Rockstar was notable not for the GTA 6 infodump that followed, but because of how it was carried out: With an Amazon Fire Stick , a mobile phone, and a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, connected to a TV in a Travelodge hotel room where he was being held under police protection because of threats against him made by rival hackers over stolen bitcoin. A 2023 assessment found Kurtaj had "acute autism" and was determined to return to "cybercrime" as soon as possible, despite the fact that he was literally standing trial for doing cybercrimes. Because of that, the jury was asked to determine if he had committed the hacks (it found he had) but not whether he had done so with criminal intent; he was subsequently sentenced to an indefinite stay at a secure hospital , where he would remain unless and until doctors determined that he was no longer a danger. As we noted at the time, "danger" might seem a bit of a strong word for someone who leaked videogame footage, but the Lapsus$ group had also hacked Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. Kurtaj was also reportedly violent while in hospital custody, causing "dozens" of reports of injuries or property damage. In July 2026, that 'no longer a danger' determination was presumably made, as Kurtaj was released from hospital and moved to prison to await retrial. He has now pleaded guilty to multiple hacks carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, including the Rockstar hack that led to the GTA 6 leak. He also pleaded guilty to assaults on workers while in custody, which the BBC report says included "multiple biting incidents." As I said when Kurtaj was moved from hospital to prison, the whole thing strikes me as odd. The big question is how Kurtaj's state of mind at the time of the crimes will influence the outcome of his guilty plea, given that a previous court determined that he needed multiple years of institutionalization. BBC tech reporter Joe Tidy, who's been following the case since Kurtaj's transfer, also described it as "an unusual move" in his report. Coincidentially, one must assume, Grand Theft Auto 6 launches for consoles on November 19. Kurtaj will be sentenced at a future date. The leaker who goes by Cyberleek , who recently distributed several GTA 6 gameplay videos apparently taken with a development build of the game, remains at large. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
sources.text: There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country. It's fitting I guess that GTA San Andreas is such a strange delight to return to. As I've waited, like everyone else, for GTA 6 , I've been back here in the GTA games of the past, via the slightly dodgy remasters from a few years ago. And what's come through for me, spending a few idle mornings messing around in San Andreas, a game I thought I knew pretty well, is how beautifully odd everything is now. The best part of 20 years have given a game that once strained against its host technology a genuine aesthetic. Surprisingly sparse in detailing, as angular and sheer as dream architecture, in love with expanses, San Andreas is perfectly placed, it seems to me, to capture just how weird California can be. California and Nevada. This is the part I always forget. I mainly think of San Andreas these days through the lens of GTA 5 , which gives you LA and its surroundings but lets the single city serve as the star. It has a bigger footprint than the earlier game, sure, but it uses that space to go deep on the detailing and the sense of a singular, fiercely specific place. San Andreas meanwhile offers three cities - and one of them isn't actually in California. Alongside spins on LA and San Francisco, you get a version of Las Vegas. It's quite neat really: the three points of some arcane spiritual triangle. The kind of thing Marvel Whiteside Parsons, aerospace engineer and Actual Wizard, might have scratched in the dust of his backyard to help him control the weather. He lived - and died - in Pasadena, so all this would have been familiar anyway. There is a classic moment in every GTA. A moment where the map opens up in the early games, or when you explore enough in the later games, and simply get to understand the audacity of what is being attempted here. In San Andreas, and this feels apt, the best way to have this moment is to break the rules, sneaking into the open map before the game is fully ready for you. An early mission allows you to step away from the critical path, as it were, and peg it to the airport in Los Santos, where a plane is waiting to be pinched. Taxi, feel the thrust, and you're off. LA beneath you - sorry, Los Santos - and on the horizon a dinkytown version of the Golden Gate Bridge and the MGM Grand. Dinkytown is the word. From the sky, the huge map of San Andreas, which still feels like an incredible piece of work - such ambition! - can look like toys laid out on a duvet in the remasters. Coming back from GTA 5, a masterpiece of texture, the cities of San Andreas in particular feel very weird - cramped and condensed and wonderfully stagey, arranged the way a kid might jury-rig them together from shoeboxes and stray cardboard. On your way out of Grove Street early on you pass the Los Santos equivalent of the Hollywood sign, looming so close the way it does in the movies but not in the actual city and you feel you could touch it. Downtown is reduced to a handful of the best buildings - it's always pleasing to see the one from the brilliant first act of Speed made the cut - but still manages to capture the important stuff too, which in this case is the way that modern LA looms somewhat cruelly over the old city, captured with a strange sepulchral dignity in the form of the City Hall, so easy to spot but now so small! Elsewhere, the ersatz Las Vega Strip looks like a drawing based on memory - a few of the classic shapes are there, but it's a sketch of a place. In this way, I guess, it captures a truth about Las Vegas. Also, perhaps, it's an admission that this is a town comfortably out of the reach of satire. As for San Francisco, it's a 60s cop movie delight to fishtail around. It nails the hills and what more do you need for a game with cars in it? Taken as a whole these cities feel mesmerising now. And it's the limitations that make them sing, I think: those sheer granite canyons of downtown LA with its towering blocks of architecture and surprisingly thin traffic, with only the very faintest of ambient soundtracks that ensures any gunfire will pop and clap and shake you out of your seat. (Remember, I am playing the remasters and sound effects may be missing.) This is the LA of Repo Man rather than Heat - an otherland where the buildings feel alien, even the air feels alien. At night, palm trees stand out against a sky that glows a deep, clean red. GTA 5 would finesse all of this, the skyboxes and whatnot, but perhaps in that finessing something is lost. (Both games, incidentally, have such a talent for capturing California's kitsch excess that they perhaps miss some of the sweeter truths, such as the astonishing diversity of cultures a city like Los Angeles finds homes for. But how could any game do that justice?) Dinkytowns aside, what San Andreas does better than GTA 5 is space - the peculiar flat spaces of Southern California in particular, a state in which you can never quite tell where the wilderness ends and the landscaping begins, and where the ancient rocks that announce the horizon can look new, like stage settings, while the freeways feel truly ancient, concrete lizards sleeping on the dirt, bleached by the easy sun. sources.title: Miami Heat shows off its 'Vice City hardwood' ahead of the big Grand Theft Auto 6 basketball game
sources.text: They've got new uniforms, too. They're pretty cool. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches at midnight on November 19 in your local time zone , meaning that people in New Zealand will be playing it while I'm still stuck at work on November 18. Unless , that is, you do your gaming on a PC, in which case GTA 6 won't be launching at all—at least, not until some indeterminate span of time has passed and Take-Two Interactive deigns to bestow it upon us. But that doesn't mean we can't indulge in all the pre-release hype, just like everyone else, and so here we are with a look at the "Vice City hardwood," upon which NBA team the Miami Heat—in the guise of the Vice City's hometown team—will square off against the Milwaukee Bucks. It's an extensive overhaul, with a huge Vice City logo at center court, the VI logos in the paint, and the "I Heart Vice City" slogans at either end. Yeah, it's marketing, but I have to admit it looks pretty cool too. Renting an entire NBA team as a promotional tool really puts a finger on just how big Grand Theft Auto 6 is. GTA 5 was big, absolutely, but GTA 6 is huge : Take-Two is looking to make something in the neighborhood of $3.5 billion in GTA 6's launch quarter alone. And it's not just the dollar signs that impress: GTA 6 is also being recognized as a mainstream cultural phenomenon in ways that previous games in the series never were, or could be. It's honestly kind of amazing how far things have come in the past 40+ years. The Vice City-ified Miami Heat will face the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, one day before the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. sources.title: Newzoo analyst expects Grand Theft Auto to turn around a rough year for console gaming: 'without GTA 6 the console market would likely be down year-over-year in 2026'
sources.text: Consoles cost more than ever, and even if you can afford to buy one you don't have as much left over to buy games for it as you used to. That's made 2026 an underwhelming year for console gaming sales, but according to the latest forecast from videogame market analysts Newzoo , the imminent launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will turn that around. "As we explored in the Global Games Market Report 2026," said Newzoo's director of market intelligence, Emmanuel Rosier, "without GTA VI the console market would likely be down year-over-year in 2026. Instead, the game's launch is expected to generate billions of dollars in revenue and give console spending a significant boost." Rosier is the analyst who, back in August, was skeptical about the idea of BioWare surviving long enough to make another Mass Effect game . I wish he'd been wrong about that, but it turned out he was right on the money with that prediction. "Western console has been losing ground," he went on to say. "Its share of global games revenue fell from 21.5% in 2015 to 17.1% in 2025, and its revenue has been broadly flat since 2021. Console adoption shows the same pattern. In Western markets, the console player base has been flat since 2022. Most people who want to play on console already do." Newzoo's prediction is that GTA 6 "will lift console full-game spending by 17.5% this year". But that's just the start of the story. "So while GTA VI is undoubtedly one of the most important releases of the decade," Rosier says, "its initial impact will be concentrated in Western console. That’s still a big market, which we forecast will be worth $36.3 billion in 2026, but it's only part of the industry. The longer-term global story will depend on what happens next, particularly on PC and online." Though tradition has plenty of people expecting a delay of roughly a year and a half between GTA 6's console and PC releases, general console malaise and the value of GTA Online—likely to be bigger on PC, and perhaps launch alongside the PC port—is a reason to think maybe the wait won't be so long. A recent GamesBeat report claims it'll be out in early 2027. "PC is far bigger than console in several major markets, including China," Rosier says, "and a PC release could expose the game to a much broader international audience. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. "The online mode is another key unknown. Depending on how it's positioned and monetized, it could significantly expand the game's audience. If Rockstar adopts a model that lowers barriers to entry, the long-term opportunity outside the traditional Western console audience could be much larger than it appears today." GTA Online was a huge part of GTA 5 's long-tail success. While Newzoo's data says at least 37% of players who preordered GTA 6 have spent money on GTA Online, only 15% did so in the last 12 months. It's in need of a refresh, and though Rockstar haven't confirmed anything, Twitch's CEO also says GTA 6's multiplayer component will be out in 2027 . sources.title: "We'd love to have you" - New Zealand's tourist board gives a nod to those hopping timezones to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early
sources.text: New Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early. "One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first." For those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result. Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 New Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it. If you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too . If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's big release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.

sources.text: My best attempt at summing up Grand Theft Auto 6 came from a conversation with a friend about something else entirely. This friend was telling me about a theory they'd recently heard, and half agreed with, that just so happened to layer over this game perfectly. Americans, they said, paraphrasing, have found a new 'third place': the car. I'm slightly skeptical of the obsession with third places these days - love the concept; less convinced that societal bonds are collapsing because today's men aren't spending enough time at their barber's. But here it felt just right: GTA 6 is, of course, a game both about America and about the personal vehicle. The clue's in the name. And as you play GTA 6, you realise, over and over, that the car is where so much of this game happens. It's where you take calls that lead to missions or story developments; where you pick up, hang out with, and chat to your partner; where you race away from police, gangs, wild animals and weirdos. Where you do much of your discovery of this properly, disorientatingly, astoundingly big and detailed world. Where you'll be when you find the most 'emergent events'. And, more than it's ever been before, the car is now an essential partner in itself; a place to stow weapons, disguises, and stolen goods - a companion it feels almost impossible to do without. I could go on about this. GTA 6 is a game of perpetual motion, as protagonists Jason and Lucia do their best to outrun a world that so often feels a step ahead - and which often culminates in some of the most exhilarating, astonishing chase sequences ever built in a video game. GTA 5 , its Los Santos-set predecessor, was aware enough of the importance of the car to name an in-game canyon after Reyner Banham, the British architectural critic who described Los Angeles' freeway system, one of the city's "four ecologies", as "Autopia". So yes: the car is the third place, in modern America and in GTA 6. The place of self-actualisation between work and home - two points that, for GTA 6's protagonists in particular, seem to always be in a state of flux. Maybe the car's their true home. For the longest time I really thought that idea summed up GTA 6 quite nicely. Until I didn't. Reducing GTA 6 to just the car, I realised, looking at it through only that one lens, forces you to be too narrow. You miss too much of it. What about the romance? The sensuality? The people and the natural world? And so what I've come to settle on instead - and honestly I expect this to change many more times over the coming days and weeks too, as even more of this horizonless game rolls back to reveal itself - is that GTA 6 just doesn't have a single thread to pull on. No one thing that, when properly grasped, suddenly draws it into a manageable shape. I've no doubt we'll all try. People have, for whatever reason, always reached for the most reductive ideas when they talk about Grand Theft Auto in particular. Maybe it's a natural response to something too big and unwieldy to instantly get your head around: to seize the first acceptable idea and declare it just 'x' . To admit something is too complex for you to immediately summarise is far less comfortable than simply dismissing it on the spot. Whatever it is, GTA 6 isn't just anything. For one, every thing it is also seems to have an opposite. It's vast - incomprehensibly vast - but also overloaded with miniscule detail. It's about big ideas, themes, places - America, society, love - and also about individuals. It's ridiculous and puerile, and also sometimes mature. Tender and violent. Deep and shallow. Novel and, in places, surprisingly familiar. It's both a big adventure playground of video game activities and a focused story of suffocating intensity. Whatever foible might arise, the game presents you with a ready-made answer - often quite literally: you can turn off notifications about your relationship status in the menu if you just want to ignore that part. You can switch to the old controls (GTA 6 has seen a bit of a control overhaul), from the first screen you're shown. Or simply tear off in the opposite direction to whatever it is that dissatisfies you and do something else. If there's an idea to reduce this game to, then, the best I can manage is this: maybe Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game designed to be irreducible. None of that is to say it's perfect. It's easy to stand in front of something like this and just bask in the awe of it, forgetting to stop a moment and step back. The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome, but there are also nits to pick. But then you step back again and they tend to fade away. GTA 6 will not be for everyone. But no game has made a better attempt at being everything. GTA 6's story begins with Jason and Lucia. Discussing it beyond that is, frankly, almost impossible to do with any kind of substance without also spoiling it. For all the precipitous leaks, Rockstar has kept its story's two most essential moments - its beginning and its end - entirely secret, and without those two moments we're only really left with euphemisms. Jason and Lucia are on the run, after a seemingly simple fetch quest goes awry. Who they're running from, or why they're being chased quite so hard, remains agonisingly beyond their field of view. But what is clear, right from the off, is exactly why they're so determined to escape. And amongst all this Rockstar has achieved something kind of momentous, when it comes to Grand Theft Auto: we've got real and very human stakes. What else can be said? Well, let's go back to Rockstar's decision to begin so explicitly with Jason and Lucia. This is a story about a relationship. You can nurture or neglect it, but fundamentally that relationship - however strong - is at the heart of things. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype
sources.text: Thirteen years later, Rockstar has crafted a worthy successor to GTA V and the new standard-bearer for open-world games. How do you follow a game like Grand Theft Auto V ? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behind Tetris and Minecraft on the list of the best-selling games of all time, and its lucrative online mode has helped it remain popular for well over a decade. That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the next GTA . A series of major leaks and delays only exacerbated this. At a time when much of the video game industry is struggling , the next edition of GTA stands alone , a cultural moment so big ( almost ) everybody has been forced to get out of the way . The buildup to Grand Theft Auto VI ’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen. Even more remarkable? The game was actually worth the wait. At this point I’ve spent nearly 80 hours in Leonida, GTA VI ’s fictional take on Florida. And what I’ve experienced is a game that combines the wide-open freedom offered in GTA V with the remarkable level of immersion from the studio’s 2018 release Red Dead Redemption 2 , while also improving on both qualities. At the same time, it’s also the most mature GTA game Rockstar has ever made, merging the criminal antics and absurdist humor the series is known for with a love story that gives you new ways to interact with the world and new reasons for wanting to push forward. This is the GTA game the studio has been building toward for its entire existence. Let’s start with that new premise. GTA V introduced the idea of multiple protagonists to the series, and VI takes that concept in a different direction. It’s a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired story about Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two small-time criminals who meet while, of course, stealing a car. It’s the most GTA -possible meet-cute. The idea is that you can play as both characters individually and also build their relationship over the course of the game. Things start out relatively slow. At the outset, Lucia is in prison, and you play solely as Jason, getting things ready for when she gets out. You can fix up your ramshackle house — that involves actually nailing down new stairs and rolling out paint on the walls — and also start building up a nest egg through means that are not exactly legal. Jason and Lucia’s relationship grows naturally over the course of the game, but it’s also a slow buildup to becoming the inseparable pair they were by the end of my playthrough. GTA VI approaches most of the experience with confident and deliberate pacing. Even when you control them individually, the characters are often together, either just hanging out or partnering for a crime. And being able to play as both is one of the game’s standout features. But I didn’t get to that point in the game until almost 17 hours in. Before that, you play as both leads mostly solo, learning who they are as people, before you’re given free rein to switch between the two. What’s great about the premise is how seamlessly it fits with what you’re actually doing in the game. There’s some bigger-picture stuff that I won’t spoil, but generally speaking, the main goal in GTA VI is to make a lot of money so that Jason and Lucia can get out of the criminal life for good and retire somewhere comfortably. And outside of the big story missions, you’re largely free to choose how you go about that. You can rob jewelry stores, steal cars, raid drug dens, or even search for hidden treasure at the bottom of the sea. Over the course of the game you’ll also meet different criminals who serve as fences, so you can sell them whatever you’ve got to build up your savings account. Sometimes they’ll even text you targets that are particularly lucrative. The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. I’m not a big fan of armed robbery, for instance. There are just so many things that can go wrong, and I almost always end up killing some innocent bystander when I try to escape. But I love getaway chases, and so stealing cars became my main form of income. Most importantly, though, this structure gives you a lot of reasons to go out in the world and explore. The missions take you all over the map — which is actually entirely accessible from the very beginning, if you choose to play that way — including not only the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City, but also tourist beaches, swamps, trailer parks, and a wild variety of other locations, each with its own landscape to explore and characters to meet. To be clear: Despite being larger, more mature, and more lifelike, this is still very much GTA . This is a game about chaos and crime. This comes across in a few ways. First, there are those smaller missions where you never really know how things will play out. The cashier at the pawn shop you’re robbing might have a shotgun, or you might accidentally smash into a big rig during a high-speed getaway. The world itself is full of unpredictable moments that force you to think on your feet. Several times I stopped my car to talk to an NPC whose vehicle broke down on the side of the road. In one instance the driver just swore at me to leave her alone. In another, I got pulled into an entire storyline involving a delivery driver who needed help to keep her AI chatbot manager off her back. I delivered her packages and ended up dealing with everything from porch pirates to tigers. The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. sources.text: GTA 6 is a game that at times feels almost embarrassingly expensive and extravagant. I cleaned a boat with a pressure washer and watched the suds build up realistically in the concrete below my characterâs flip-flops. I ran through a tram station and spotted over 100 different NPCs milling about, all unique and all moving. Hair gets wet. Sweat builds up on backs. Even for Rockstar, the master of tiny details, GTA 6 is overflowing with examples of what happens when you let a studio work on one game for a decade. Itâs a lot, but it all serves the purpose of creating a virtual world that players can truly get lost in.Â Iâve put over 150 hours into GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 Pro, and I expect Iâll spend even more time in this digital recreation of Florida and Miami, as thereâs so much to do and see in Vice City. I doubt most players will see half of it. I bet I wonât ever see it all.Â GTA 6 is a massive third-person open-world game, like Rockstarâs previous offerings. It merges the slower pace and slice-of-life mechanics from Red Dead Redemption 2 with the urban sprawl and crime-movie feel of GTA IV and GTA V . Itâs a more grounded journey than its predecessors, one which requires more planning and consideration if you want to survive and succeed as modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, robbing small stores as you work your way up to bigger scores, like banks. Itâs often a tougher game than any past GTA , but in a way that rewards skill and patience. Or bravery, stupidity, and luck.Â I have quibbles about some clunky controls and some story pacing problems in the gameâs later chapters, but like crappy cupholders in a million-dollar supercar, they donât really get in the way of what’s here. Instead, they’re minor issues to point at as I hit the gas and go 200 MPH with the radio blasting.Â The best part of Grand Theft Auto 6 isnât what I expected. It’s not the crime, or the action, or the massive world to explore, though all of those parts are excellent and better than ever. The real standout of GTA 6 , the part of the game that kept me hooked and which I wonât forget anytime soon, is its central duo, Jason and Lucia. Not only do they have very different motivations than past GTA protagonists, wanting to create a better life for themselves and escape their life of crime instead of vying to become crime lords or get revenge, but they are easily Rockstarâs most fully fleshed-out, believable, and relatable characters. At the start of the game, Jason and Lucia are separated after a short relationship. Lucia tried to rob a payday loan place after breaking up with Jason and, in the process, got arrested. This moment has huge ramifications for both of their lives and ultimately pulls them together early on in GTA 6 âs runtime. Jason, an Army vet, is more reserved than your average GTA protagonist. Heâs a loyal man who’s conflicted about the things he does to get by and try to make things better for himself and Lucia. A lot of people tell Jason heâs a good guy, but heâs never sure if he really is. Meanwhile, Lucia, a petty thief living paycheck to paycheck, knows sheâs flawed and doesnât care nearly as much as Jason about that fact. Sheâs more focused on improving her life by any means and has a bigger goal that drives her to take bigger risks.Â Together they balance each other out, with Jason often acting as a voice of reason and Lucia pushing him to strive for more. Their dynamic is unlike anything Iâve seen in a Rockstar-developed game, and thanks to some stellar writing and performances, I found myself deeply caring about these two criminals just trying to make it.Â Throughout the entire run of GTA 6 , Jason and Lucia interact as you would expect two real people who care for each other would. They joke with each other, comment on events happening around them, share secrets, and help each other when they can.Â Spending time with them is never annoying. Neither Lucia nor Jason pesters the player when youâre hanging around with them in the open world. Sometimes they might point out that you missed a turn or a possible way to sneak into a gang-infested hideout. This never felt like some annoying video-gamey handholding, just a couple working together.Â While Jason and Lucia are both skilled at stealing cars, shooting guns, and running around causing chaos, they arenât always treated as equals in the world. While playing as Lucia, I was hit on by random assholes and catcalled by men on the street. It wasnât constant, but it happened enough that it was impossible to ignore. Some characters will also doubt Luciaâs abilities, but never question Jasonâs skills as a murderous criminal. It adds an intriguing wrinkle to playing as either character. Lucia feels like she has to work harder to prove herself among her criminal peers. Jason often has her back in these scenarios, but lets her hold her own, and she does so with sharp words and strong punches.Â Even outside of when they directly speak to each other to tell stories or give feedback, the other’s presence is always felt, sometimes in small gestures, like one holding the door for the other as they enter a building. sources.text: More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time . Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans. But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players. Lost in the excitement of GTA VI finally launching is the fact that Rockstar employees are in the process of voting on whether or not to unionize. Developer Nestor Uriarte explains the importance of the moment in an essay in The Guardian : Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that. As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more. Now that reviews have dropped for the game, it has skyrocketed to the top of Metacritic’s highest-rated list , surpassing Ocarina of Time (the original, not the remake ). Of course, this could change as more reviews trickle in, but for now it’s safe to say that GTA VI was worth the long wait. Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just the biggest GTA game to date; it’s also the most romantic. Though the series is well known for its sordid assortment of criminal leads, GTA VI switches things up by starring a pair of thieves who also happen to fall in love after meeting while stealing a car. It’s still an open-world action game full of chaos and mayhem. But many players will also be attempting to nurture the budding relationship in between heists. The sprawling game is designed to support both audiences. “It’s a risk,” explains Rob Nelson, producer on GTA VI and co-studio head at developer Rockstar North. “It’s a real change for Grand Theft Auto . You can still play it the old way, you can reject all of this stuff. But for people who do engage, it’s meaningful — you’re earning it, you’re working at it, just like in a normal relationship.” How do you follow a game like Grand Theft Auto V ? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behind Tetris and Minecraft on the list of the best-selling games of all time, and its lucrative online mode has helped it remain popular for well over a decade. That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the next GTA . A series of major leaks and delays only exacerbated this. At a time when much of the video game industry is struggling , the next edition of GTA stands alone , a cultural moment so big ( almost ) everybody has been forced to get out of the way . The buildup to Grand Theft Auto VI ’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen. Sony has confirmed the 1.267GB download is mandatory to play the new Grand Theft Auto when it launches at midnight tonight. As with most PlayStation firmware patches, we don’t know what it does though, beyond “some security fixes to the system software.” Rockstar hasn’t publicly said who is playing the two leads in GTA VI , but The Game Awards’ nominee video says that Manni L. Perez has been nominated for Best Performance for her work in the game. GTA VI earned eight nominations , the most of any title, including one for Game of the Year . Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other big companies, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS). Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the company “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS says.

sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 GTA 6 GTA 7 Rockstar Games After a very long wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here. And the new game contains a joke that pokes fun at how long it took Rockstar to make GTA 6 and also references the franchise’s past and future. In GTA 6 , players can scroll through Snapmatic, an Instagram-like social media platform found on Jason and Lucia’s in-game phones. Snapmatic contains hundreds and hundreds of posts, videos, and comments. As you play the game, more posts are added as people react to the events of GTA 6 and also just post memes, conspiracies, funny videos, and other random junk. And very early in the game, if you check Snapmatic, you can find a post complaining that gamers in the world of GTA 6 got a video game based on an in-universe kids’ cartoon before Race and Chase 7. For those not aware, Race and Chase is a reference to Grand Theft Auto ‘s original name. Before the original top-down GTA became what we know today, it started life as a game that would have let players race around as street racers or chase down those drivers as cops. Hence the name Race’n’Chase . As the idea evolved, so did the name. It seems very likely that Race and Chase 7 is a nod to GTA 7. And the post on Snapmatic joking about getting a Barnyard Blue video game before Race and Chase 7 seems to be Rockstar acknowledging the years of people posting comments online like “I can’t believe we got [insert game sequel/remake/etc] before GTA 6 .” Apparently, in the world of GTA 6, gamers have been waiting a long time to play the new Race and Chase. I understand their collective pain. This isn’t the first time Race and Chase has popped up in a GTA game , either. In GTA Online , players can find and play three variants of an arcade racing game titled Race and Chase . If we assume those are the first three games in the series, then I’d assume that RAC 4 and RAC 5 moved the franchise away from being just a basic arcade racing game and into something big enough to have people super-hyped for Race and Chase 7. sources.text: Well, whaddaya know? Turns out all you need to make a great videogame is around a decade of time, the GDP of a BRICS nation, and a marketing machine pervasive to the point of totalitarianism. The reviews for Grand Theft Auto 6 —Rockstar's sequel to that game that would splash " GOURANGA !" on the screen when you ran over enough people—are in. People like it a lot. No, really, they're out of their gourd for this one, folks. GTA 6 might just be the most absurdly hyped game in history, and yet the mad lads at Rockstar really seem to have pulled it off. Of course, the game's true test—its review on PC Gamer dot com and its accompanying magazine—hasn't happened yet. We'll have to wait for the all-but-certain PC port for that. For now, you can read our impressions of the console version here . But our console brethren have been putting pen to paper to get their thoughts down, and the reviews for GTA 6 are flowing thick and fast. Here's a sample platter of them, to give you an idea of just how nuts people are going for this thing. GameSpot's Tamoor Hussain paints a picture of Leonida that overflows with detail, calling it "a game of staggering scope and scale obsessed with small details that could be lost in its vastness, a giant haystack full of needles that you’ll constantly find, creating delight in their improbable discovery". I get the impression that a year from now, five years, ten years, there will still be people rushing to subreddits and forums (if we still have those) to ask if others have seen this or that little detail Rockstar tucked into some obscure corner of its humungous world. A second perfect score from the gang at IGN, whose Luke Reilly had a great time doing things like: Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Most of which you could feasibly cram into a game whose goal was to simulate my dad, but in GTA 6 it all forms part of a world that constantly surprises you with things to do. "I see no real limit to the amount of time I could spend here, endlessly exploring and interacting with Vice City and the massive area surrounding it", writes Reilly, adding that—despite having beaten the game with 120 hours of playtime under his belt—"While the well-paced story effectively nudged me around the map, there are still vast sections of it that I’m yet to even visit". Our brothers in arms at GR note that GTA 6 is an improvement on every entry in the series before it: "there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments", writes Josh West, who calls the game (affectionately) "the ultimate time vampire" where "every one of your actions ultimately impacts the lives of Jason and Lucia". Honestly, sounds like a nerve-wracking amount of responsibility for me. The New York Times – Too stately to give a review score but it's an "NYT Critic’s Pick" You know a videogame has broken containment when the grey lady is getting in on the review beat. The NYT's Yussef Cole zeroed in on GTA 6's heart in his review: the relationship between protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos—"This is a game about love and relationships, their joy and heartache, and the work required to make them successful", he writes, noting that players can choose to hold hands with their paramour at the touch of a button. We've come a little ways from beating people to death with dildos, folks (though you may well still be able to do that; I'd be surprised if you couldn't). Giant Bomb (shoutout to Charlie Tunoku) joins in with the hosannahs for GTA 6, describing it as one of those games that feels like a step up for the medium as a whole. "Grand Theft Auto VI is Rockstar’s best game", writes Dan Ryckert. "In the thirteen years between entries of one of the biggest franchises in entertainment, fans’ expectations grew to a level that felt unrealistic. Somehow, Rockstar has managed to overdeliver on the most hyped video game of all time". The Guardian's Keza MacDonald writes that Rockstar's Leonida is so realistic as to defy belief, but that in its humid, gator-ridden byways you will find scope for both "foulmouthed, OTT chaos—as well as new empathy for the fugitive couple at its centre". It is a game, it seems, that is almost too big and varied to squeeze into something like a regular review. "it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start". But you bet those experiences are many, varied, and shockingly fleshed-out. Bloomberg – Unscored, but you get the picture Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, who you may recognise from videogame scoops, is in love with GTA 6 too. He opens with a description of one of the random events that can happen to players in the game, in which he witnessed a crash and found himself enlisted into an NPC's scam to sue a parody of Amazon for millions. "Incidents like this, elaborate depictions of a heightened reality, happen constantly in Grand Theft Auto 6", he writes. "The joy of Grand Theft Auto VI, much like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Elden Ring before it, comes from discovering its world’s delights and seeing how it reacts to your actions". It perhaps tells us something that the only non-perfect score on this list is… a 4.5/5 overflowing with praise. Slant's Justin Clark calls GTA 6 "something above and beyond anything the AAA gaming space has ever produced", and has oodles of praise for its rich and hyper-detailed open world. sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is the US' best-selling physical game so far this year
sources.text: The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game , Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail. The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom . That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years. While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026 , and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028 . Ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post , Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere. In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

sources.text: The GTA 6 Metacritic score is here, and perhaps unsurprisingly, it's not only the highest rated game of 2026, but the highest-rated game of all time. If you look at the Metacritic "Best Games of All Time" list , there's a couple things you're going to notice – namely, Nintendo and Rockstar Games , or more specifically, Mario, Zelda, and Grand Theft Auto. And now joining GTA 4 and GTA 5 as one of the highest-rated games of all time is GTA 6, with reviews awarding it a score of 99 after 107 reviews. This makes it the highest rated game of 2026, and matches the original N64 release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated game ever. You just need to look at the GamesRadar+ GTA 6 review to see why, with editor-in-chief Josh West awarding the latest Rockstar Games title 5/5, saying "Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality," and adding that "there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments." Perhaps unsurprisingly, there's a lot of outlets giving Rockstar's latest full marks, with the likes of IGN, TechRadar Gaming, Edge, and Game Informer being among the many outlets giving the max score. And as of right now there are no reviews that Metacritic classes as "Negative," or even "Mixed" for that matter. Obviously, this Metacritic score and the game's eight nominations at The Game Awards 2026 is just the cherry on top for Rockstar, as the game is already estimated to have made $1.45 billion from pre-orders alone , and as the game releases in New Zealand right about now, I imagine that number will be far surpassed as people dig into the game. sources.text: Includes the return of Now & Later Packs, MLB The Show 26 community stats, and more. Before we dive into new information on MLB The Show 27, let’s take a look back. As we reflect on 2026, two things stand out above everything else: the incredible passion and support of the MLB The Show community, and our need to better communicate and react to community feedback going forward. Whether you’ve been playing for decades or joined us for the first time this year, you’ve helped make this another special chapter in our franchise’s history. While we’re proud of what our team accomplished this year, we recognize that the heart of MLB The Show has always been its community. Since launch, you’ve hit an astonishing: You’ve also drawn 123,300,616 walks and racked up a staggering 2,130,551,161 strikeouts. It seems we have some work to do on our collective plate discipline and pitch recognition! But it’s not all strikeouts. You’ve also recorded 18,666,758 Perfect-Perfect hits and scored an incredible 2,506,757,548 runs. And if those numbers weren’t impressive enough, the community collectively spent the equivalent of 31,541 years playing MLB The Show this year. This year was not without some issues and hopefully over the next few months we’ll show you how we’ve made improvements in a host of areas.Your stories, feedback, creativity, and passion remind us why we do what we do. We don’t take your time, trust, or support for granted, and we’re incredibly fortunate to have a community that cares so deeply about the game. From all of us at San Diego Studio, thank you for another unforgettable year. We’re excited about what lies ahead and look forward to continuing this journey together. So, what lies ahead? We’re eager to share the exciting new features and improvements coming to MLB The Show 27, but it’s still a little too early to reveal what’s in store. However, there’s one announcement we can’t wait to make: The Tech Test is officially returning for MLB The Show 27. Tech Tests are invaluable to the development process. They help our team identify bugs, evaluate performance, and gather meaningful feedback from the community before the game officially launches. Now, you might be wondering: If Tech Tests are so important, why haven’t we held one since MLB The Show 23? That’s a fair question. Game development is challenging, and each year brings its own set of difficult decisions and competing priorities. Some of those decisions resulted in us not holding Tech Tests for the past few years. We appreciate your patience, passion, and continued support, and we’re looking forward to having you be part of the process again. We will provide more details on the Tech Test in the new year. There is still more ahead for MLB The Show 26 , and the time you spend playing can give you a head start in MLB The Show 27. Now & Later packs are coming back. Now & Later Packs contain items you can use now in MLB The Show 26, with the added bonus of allowing you to redeem The Show Packs “later” in MLB The Show 27 at no additional cost. Each Now & Later Pack you earn playing Diamond Dynasty Content in MLB The Show 26 on console will give out a Now & Later voucher that will automatically be redeemed into The Show Packs when logging into MLB The Show 27 on console during its standard release. Make sure you log into ‘27 with the same account you used to earn Now & Later Packs in ‘26. While that’s all for today, in the meantime, get a head start and start earning those Now & Later Packs in MLB The Show 26. We look forward to sharing more soon and are excited about what’s to come in 2027. In the meantime, for the latest MLB The Show news, head to TheShow.com , sign up for The Scouting Report , and follow our official social channels.

sources.title: GTA 6 Jason and Lucia Relationship Guide—How To Build Your Bond, Explained
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 features two playable characters: Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. From the opening sequences of the game, you learn how they found each other and what they’re fighting for. As the game unfolds, you’ll need to build that relationship, working through the levels and shaping your story together. If you neglect that relationship, you’ll see cracks start to form, and you’ll ultimately impact how the game plays out. If you nurture the relationship, things will go in the opposite direction. In this guide, learn about the relationship levels in GTA 6 and how you can maintain your relationship. There are four relationship levels in GTA 6, and they’re fairly indicative of what they mean by how they’re named: There’s no breakup about to happen in GTA 6, so don’t worry about hitting a 0/4. That doesn’t exist. If you want to build your relationship, you’ll need to spend time together. That sounds simple enough, but what you do matters. There are mechanics built into the game, such as saying hello when you meet up, holding your partner’s hand, or offering to pay for something, that slowly build the bond. If you do more ambitious activities together, such as playing sports, taking a drive, embarking on a leisure activity, or going off the deep end and robbing some place together , you’ll see that bond building much faster. It’s a two-way street, though. Both Jason and Lucia will need to contribute to the relationship. That means you’ll need to switch character from time to time to carry out those affectionate actions (hold RIGHT on the d-pad and hit RB/R1). If you want to sour the relationship in GTA 6 deliberately , there’s plenty you can do… Unfortunately. For instance, if you flat-out ignore phone calls and messages, spend hours upon hours apart, or quite literally abandon your partner when you’re out exploring, you’ll see a massive drop in your relationship level. It gets worse if you bring harm to your partner, allow them to be pursued by the police, or anything in that ballpark. You’ll see things rapidly degrade if this happens. So, you see, it’s relatively easy to maintain your relationship in GTA 6. Just go about it as you would a real-world relationship, remember to approach the concept with both characters, and make sure you’re taking care of the little things. Easy! sources.title: Sony Issues Official PS5 Firmware Update Warning, Confirms GTA 6 Requirement
sources.text: Sony has confirmed that the recently released PS5 firmware 14.23 update is required to play GTA 6, in a social media post boosted by Rockstar Games. Yesterday November 17, Sony released PS5 system software update 26.07-14.23.00 , which weighed in at 1.267 GB. According to Sony’s official patch notes, it makes “some security fixes to the system software.” Now, just hours before GTA 6 launches at midnight across the world, the PlayStation Support U.S. X / Twitter account confirmed what many had suspected: “Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19.” The official Rockstar Games account then reposted it to its 23.7 million followers. It is believed this unprecedented PS5 update cuts PlayStation Network access to older firmware, which means if you haven’t upgraded to 14.23 you will not be able to play GTA 6 on PS5. 14.23 released just a day after a prominent PS5 hacker claimed to be the first person to have “dumped” a game binary at 14.22, although they did not share any jailbreak. The PlayStation homebrew scene has made headlines in the last two months for releasing PS5 jailbreaks for prior firmwares. For example, late September, a jailbreak that supported all PS5 consoles running firmware 7.00-13.60 sent shockwaves through the homebrew community because, at the time, it meant that all PS5s, including the PS5 Pro, that hadn't been updated within the previous week were compatible with the jailbreak. This was of huge significance for Sony and the security of the PS5, as people with a jailbroken PS5 can modify their console, potentially opening the door to video game piracy. However, it was found that some PS5 games subsequently required the more recent 14.00 firmware in order to download updates, sparking a renewed effort to release a new jailbreak for the updated system software. So, there is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security. This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak was made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC. The question for Sony is whether it can do enough to eventually win this game of Whac-A-Mole with the homebrew scene. This is something of an existential crisis for Sony, which publishers and developers rely upon for the security of their PlayStation releases. But with the emergence of powerful AI models, the stakes have risen significantly. Just last week, Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, told IGN that the company was taking security seriously , and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version. During an investor-focused Q&A, Zelnick was asked multiple times about this AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up. “This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations. “That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.” GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and some companies have even given staff bonus time off to play it . We've got plenty more on GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 launch, including details on the New Zealand trick people are using to play early, Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research , and — finally — confirmation of the actress who plays Lucia . sources.title: Sony squeezes out a PlayStation 5 firmware update before the release of GTA 6
sources.text: Sony has managed to squeeze out another PlayStation 5 firmware update before the highly-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto 6 . Sony has been rolling firmware updates out on a fairly regular basis, and like many of those updates, this latest one - version 26.07-14.23.00 - doesn't bring any very meaningful changes. Sony repeated the same "we've made some security fixes to the system software" patch-note that we've seen many times before. And like all those firmware updates, 26.07-14.23.00 is mandatory for all PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles, assuming you want to go online or play the latest games. That, of course, includes GTA 6 , which requires the console's firmware to be updated to its latest version before you can play. The update should download automatically the next time you turn on your console, but you can also force the download through Settings > System > System Software > System Software Update and Settings. This is also where you can tick the option for your console to automatically download and install those updates in the future. Although Sony hasn't directly said so, the high frequency of those security firmware updates is likely related to the impending release of GTA 6, especially in light of recent gen-AI-driven PS5 jailbreaks . Any firmware released before GTA 6's release now becomes required to play the game, which delays potential security exploits, seeing as hackers would need to find vulnerabilities in that firmware in order to play. While this may never happen, Sony is at least trying to minimise the risk as much as possible. GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

sources.text: "Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19," Sony says Hours before the worldwide launch of GTA 6 , Sony has rolled out a new PS5 system update that's mandatory to play Rockstar's upcoming blockbuster – and I can't help but wonder if it's in an effort to stop the inevitable attempts to dump the game on jailbroken hardware. PS5 firmware update 26.07-14.23.00 rolled out yesterday, with patch notes that give incredibly little away: "We've made some security fixes to the system software." However, a follow-up post from the official PlayStation Support account on Twitter may shed a bit more light on the situation. "Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI," it reads. "Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they're ready to play on launch day, November 19." Before updating, you'll also find yourself unable to use PSN features, so you'll want to get this one installed as soon as possible if you're wanting to use your console properly and, of course, dive into GTA 6. While Sony hasn't said it directly, many folks are assuming that this mandatory update is the company's attempt to crack down on GTA 6 piracy before it happens. Recent months have seen huge developments in the PS5 jailbreaking scene , with one of the most prominent members reporting just days ago ( thanks, VideoCardz ) that they'd been able to dump "game binary at PS5 14.22," the previous firmware version to yesterday's update. They didn't say if the game in question was GTA 6, and their Twitter account has since vanished, but obviously, it left some to wonder if Rockstar's game might be dumped soon after launch by anyone who could work out the same exploit and take it further. Well, it's a reasonable conclusion that Sony's latest update could, in theory, slow down any attempts to do so. Recently, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said that "this business has been largely immune to piracy concerns," but admitted that in the age of AI-powered recompilations, it's "going to become more of a challenge." Even so, he said: "I think it will be manageable, and we are focused on it." sources.title: Atualização da Sony pode ser obrigatória para jogar GTA 6 no PS5
sources.text: A Sony liberou nesta terça-feira (17) uma atualização de sistema para o PlayStation 5 e o PS5 Pro às vésperas da chegada de Grand Theft Auto VI . Identificado como versão 26.07-14.23.00, o pacote tem 1,267 GB e traz correções de segurança. A liberação ocorre um dia após um integrante da comunidade de desbloqueio afirmar ter extraído dados de um jogo na versão anterior, a 14.22. A empresa não detalhou quais vulnerabilidades foram corrigidas no novo firmware. Nas notas oficiais, a Sony resume as mudanças em uma única frase: “Fizemos algumas correções de segurança no software do sistema”. Sem a atualização , o console fica impedido de acessar recursos online, baixar atualizações pela PlayStation Network e executar títulos recentes. A atualização foi liberada um dia depois de o pesquisador conhecido como Gezine afirmar, em 16 de novembro, que havia conseguido extrair o executável de um jogo rodando no firmware 14.22. Ele não revelou o nome do título nem publicou o arquivo na internet. Após a declaração, Gezine apagou sua conta na rede social X, sem explicar publicamente a decisão. O programador EchoStretch afirmou ter conversado com ele sobre o afastamento da comunidade, mas não revelou o motivo. Segundo relatos da comunidade, desenvolvedores também vêm utilizando ferramentas de inteligência artificial generativa para mapear brechas na arquitetura de software do PS5 com mais rapidez. Apesar da proximidade entre os acontecimentos, não há confirmação oficial de que a versão 14.23 seja uma resposta direta ao caso envolvendo o firmware 14.22. As informações sobre a exigência do novo firmware para GTA 6 são divergentes. Metadados anteriores do pré-carregamento indicavam a versão 14.22 como requisito mínimo. A primeira fonte afirma que a Sony passou a exigir a atualização antes do lançamento, inclusive de quem já havia baixado o jogo antecipadamente. A segunda, porém, informa que essa obrigatoriedade ainda não foi confirmada oficialmente pela Sony ou pela Rockstar Games. Independentemente dessa exigência, e para não correr nenhum risco de o jogo não rodar, os usuários podem verificar se o console já recebeu o novo firmware. Caso o download automático não tenha sido iniciado, a atualização pode ser instalada manualmente pelo menu do sistema: Quando conectado à internet, o PS5 também pode baixar o pacote automaticamente.
